summary: Phase D backend tests (Multi-branch Locations + Bulk Product Upload) — 19/19 pytest cases PASS. Verified public GET /api/locations returns both seeded locations (Design Center Mumbai, Registered Office Ernakulam) sorted by order, admin CRUD flow (create → PATCH deactivate hides from public → DELETE removes), template.csv download with real DB category slugs in '#' instruction rows, bulk upload happy path (existing sku updated + new sku created), row-level error handling (bad category_slug / missing name / missing sku+slug / price<=0), UTF-8 BOM (Google Sheets export style), XLSX via openpyxl, '#' comment rows correctly ignored, plus regression sanity on /api/products (paginated {items,total}), /api/categories, HOPE10 coupon and admin 401. All test-created products and locations cleaned up via mongosh teardown.

minor.issue: Now returns paginated {items:[], total:N} instead of a bare list. Existing bulk-upload feature works fine — test suite was adjusted to handle both shapes. If Phase C test file (test_phase_c_orders.py) or the frontend consumes the bare-list contract, it may need to be updated.
Returns 200 (not 201) on create. Not incorrect, just noting convention — 201 Created is more RESTful.
Returns 200 with {ok:true} even when id does not exist (no 404). Idempotent-by-design; acceptable but worth documenting.
Ends with a trailing/blank CSV row (writer.writerow([])). Harmless — parses fine — but a stray empty line in the downloaded template may look odd to users. Consider removing.

action_items: None blocking. All Phase D acceptance criteria are verified end-to-end.
(Optional) Return 201 on POST /api/admin/locations for REST correctness.
(Optional) Return 404 from DELETE /api/admin/locations/{id} when id is missing so callers can distinguish 'deleted' vs 'not found'.
(Optional) Strip the empty writer.writerow([]) from template.csv to avoid a trailing blank row.
(Awareness) /api/products response shape changed to {items,total,...}. Ensure Phase C test file and any frontend/product-listing code handle this correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1422 lines — well over the 700-line soft cap and up ~230 lines since Phase C. Strongly recommend splitting: locations.py, bulk_upload.py, orders.py, admin.py etc.

bulk_upload_products: `_parse_int` silently coerces float strings and comma-thousands, but returns default=None on non-numeric — which is caught by the price<=0 branch. However non-numeric `stock` or `original_price` silently become 0/price. Consider surfacing these as row errors.

bulk_upload_products: `image` falls back to a hard-coded Unsplash URL. If Unsplash link-rot happens, all bulk-imported products with empty image will point to a broken URL. Consider a locally-hosted placeholder in /public and store its relative path.
bulk_upload_products: no explicit content-length/upload-size limit on `file` — a maliciously large XLSX could OOM the worker. Consider `file.size` check + streaming for very large sheets.

bulk_upload_products: iterates rows sequentially with `await` per row (~2 DB roundtrips each). For large sheets this will be slow. Consider batching: gather existing SKUs/slugs in one query, insertMany/bulkWrite the rest.

delete_location: does not surface `not-found` vs `deleted` (returns 200 either way). Also does not check if the location is `is_primary` — a user could accidentally delete their primary branch. Consider preventing deletion of is_primary=true locations, or auto-promoting the next one.

public_locations sort uses `.sort('order', 1)` only — no secondary tie-breaker. Two locations with the same `order` value will have non-deterministic ordering across restarts. Recommend `.sort([('order',1),('created_at',1)])`.

update_location accepts arbitrary `dict` payload without Pydantic validation — a caller could set `id`, `_id` (both popped, good) or any other field, but also could send `active: 'no'` (string) and it would be stored as-is. Recommend a `LocationUpdate` Pydantic model.

download_product_template response has hard-coded fallback slug list in the `else` branch that no longer matches the actual DB (missing head-gear, wall-frames, jewellery, etc.). Since DB is always seeded this branch is unreachable, but if it did fire it would mislead users. Remove the else fallback and just leave empty.

PRODUCT_TEMPLATE_COLUMNS declared but never used to enforce/validate headers in `_read_upload_rows` — an uploaded CSV with a misspelled column will silently be ignored (e.g., `catgory_slug` → row will fail with 'Unknown category_slug'). Consider validating headers up-front and returning a top-level error.
test_credentials: Admin session minted via mongosh at test session start (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Fresh Bearer token per pytest session.
seed_data_creation: During the test session the suite creates: (a) 1 test location (label='Test Branch', Bangalore) — created via POST then DELETEd by the same test, (b) 6 test products with SKUs starting PYTEST-BULK-* — deleted in autouse session-scoped teardown via mongosh. Verified via mongosh post-run: 0 PYTEST-* products remain, 0 'Test Branch' locations remain, both seeded locations (loc_01, loc_02) intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: `cd /app/backend && set -a && source .env && set +a && python -m pytest tests/test_phase_d_locations_bulk.py -v -n 0`. Force `-n 0` (serial) — the bulk-upload tests share test-data state via the module-level _created_product_skus list which the autouse session teardown reads. /api/products returns paginated {items,total,page,limit}; do NOT assume bare list. Categories in DB (verified): drinkware, clothing, bags, head-gear, boards, tags, badges-magnets, stickers, jewellery, wall-frames.
rca of the issue: N/A — no backend bugs surfaced. Initial test run had 2 test-side issues: (1) /api/products response shape is paginated {items,total} but the initial test assumed bare list — fixed test to handle both, (2) same underlying issue in the bulk-upload happy-path test when discovering an existing SKU. Both were test-infra bugs, not application bugs.
